bib.title: HuggingGPT: Solving AI Tasks with ChatGPT and its Friends in Hugging Face

read.skipped: Reference list and case-study figure text skimmed only

question: Can an LLM act as a controller that plans tasks and selects and runs expert models from Hugging Face to solve complex multimodal AI tasks through language as the interface?
hypothesis: LLMs can manage existing AI models via language descriptions to solve complicated AI tasks.
contributions: HuggingGPT with an inter-model cooperation protocol, LLM as the brain for planning and decision
Integration of the Hugging Face hub for multimodal, multi-domain tasks
Evaluations of LLM capability in task planning and model selection
Experiments across language, vision, speech and cross-modality tasks

method.summary: A controller LLM (ChatGPT) runs four stages: task planning into a JSON task graph with dependencies, model selection from Hugging Face model descriptions (filtered by task type, top-K by downloads), task execution (parallel when independent, hybrid local/cloud endpoints), and response generation. Evaluated on task-planning quality across LLMs and a 130-request human evaluation.
method.task: LLM-controlled orchestration of expert models for multimodal AI tasks

datasets.name: GPT-4-annotated task planning set
datasets.source: requests submitted by annotators, labels (pseudo) from GPT-4

datasets.source: manually created from 3-5 tasks of the task list

other.note: named as a main LLM; no results reported

inference.prompting: Three prompts (Table 1): task planning with slots Available Task List, Demonstrations, Chat Logs; model selection with Candidate Models; response generation. Few-shot demonstrations (0 to 5 shots in ablation; default number not stated).
inference.retrieval: Model selection: filter models by task type, rank by Hugging Face downloads, take top-K candidates (K not stated)

parameters.logit_bias: 0.2 on format tokens such as { and }

other.parallelism: tasks without unmet dependencies run in parallel

metrics.name: Accuracy / Precision / Recall / F1
metrics.definition: task-name match for planning; type only, arguments ignored

metrics.name: Edit Distance (ED)
metrics.definition: normalized edit distance between planned and reference task sequences

metrics.name: GPT-4 Score
metrics.definition: GPT-4 judges whether a planned graph is accurate (yes/no), accuracy of its judgments

metrics.name: Passing rate / Rationality / Success rate
metrics.definition: three human experts rate whether plan or model runs, fits the request, and final result satisfies the user; averaged

eval.protocol: Planning scored against GPT-4 pseudo-labels and a small human-annotated set; human evaluation by three experts on 130 requests; no seeds or significance tests stated.

prompts.text: #1 Task Planning Stage - The AI assistant performs task parsing on user input, generating a list of tasks with the following format: [{"task": task, "id", task_id, "dep": dependency_task_ids, "args": {"text": text, "image": URL, "audio": URL, "video": URL}}]. The "dep" field denotes the id of the previous task which generates a new resource upon which the current task relies. The tag "<resource>-task_id" represents the generated text, image, audio, or video from the dependency task with the corresponding task_id. The task must be selected from the following options: {{ Available Task List }}. Please note that there exists a logical connections and order between the tasks. In case the user input cannot be parsed, an empty JSON response should be provided. Here are several cases for your reference: {{ Demonstrations }}. To assist with task planning, the chat history is available as {{ Chat Logs }}, where you can trace the user-mentioned resources and incorporate them into the task planning stage.

#2 Model Selection Stage - Given the user request and the call command, the AI assistant helps the user to select a suitable model from a list of models to process the user request. The AI assistant merely outputs the model id of the most appropriate model. The output must be in a strict JSON format: {"id": "id", "reason": "your detail reason for the choice"}. We have a list of models for you to choose from {{ Candidate Models }}. Please select one model from the list.

#4 Response Generation Stage - With the input and the inference results, the AI assistant needs to describe the process and results. The previous stages can be formed as - User Input: {{ User Input }}, Task Planning: {{ Tasks }}, Model Selection: {{ Model Assignment }}, Task Execution: {{ Predictions }}. You must first answer the user's request in a straightforward manner. Then describe the task process and show your analysis and model inference results to the user in the first person. If inference results contain a file path, must tell the user the complete file path. If there is nothing in the results, please tell me you can't make it.

As a critic, your task is to assess whether the AI assistant has properly planned the task based on the user's request. ... {"choice": "yes"/"no", "reason": "Your reason for your choice"} ... Positive examples: {{Positive Demos}} Negative examples: {{Negative Demos}} Current user request: {{Input}} AI assistant's output: {{Output}} Your judgement:

limits: Planning depends on the LLM; plans may be infeasible or suboptimal
Multiple LLM calls per request raise latency
Context length limits how many model descriptions fit
Instability: LLM may not follow format or instructions
Planning scored on task type only, arguments ignored; GPT-4 Score is not always correct
Human-annotated set has only 46 examples; K, default shot count and cost are not stated
Sec 4.1 names text-davinci-003 but reports no results for it
